# ExpressiveCSS extras component decisions

Components of `@expressivecss/extras`, outside the Material 3 component set. Alternatives marked (core) have guides in the `expressivecss` skill. Search for the job's terms, then read the matching row's guide. Compare alternatives (component slugs) only when the fit is ambiguous.

| Component | Use when | Avoid when | Alternatives | Runtime |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Footer](../components/footer.md) | Site links and legal information at page end. | Primary app destinations need persistent navigation. | navigation-bar (core) | css-only |
| [Stepper](../components/stepper.md) | Show progress through a fixed order of steps the user completes one after another. | Views people switch between freely need tabs; one task with a percentage needs a progress indicator. | tabs (core), progress (core), breadcrumbs (core), timeline, questionnaire | css-only |
| [Mega menu](../components/mega-menu.md) | Give a site with many sections top-level navigation whose items open panels of grouped links. | Commands in an application belong in a menu or menubar; a short list of destinations needs a navbar or navigation rail. | menu (core), menubar, app-bar (core) | css-only |
| [Tree](../components/tree.md) | Browse a hierarchy several levels deep, such as files or nested sections, with branches that open in place. | One or two levels of navigation need a navigation rail or a list; peer sections need tabs. | lists (core), navigation-rail (core), accordion (core), org-chart | native |
| [Menubar](../components/menubar.md) | Give an application, such as an editor, a persistent row of command menus people move through with the arrow keys. | Site navigation needs a navbar or mega menu of links; a single overflow of actions needs one menu. | menu (core), toolbars (core), mega-menu | auto-init |
| [Scrollspy](../components/scrollspy.md) | Track visible sections in a table of contents. | Separate views need navigation or tabs. | tabs (core), navigation-bar (core) | auto-init |
| [Back to top](../components/back-to-top.md) | Give readers of a long article, docs page or feed a way back to the top and its navigation without scrolling the whole way. | Pages shorter than a few screens, or content that scrolls inside a pane or dialog rather than the window. | fab (core), scrollspy | auto-init |
| [Aura](../components/aura.md) | Draw the eye to the single most important button, card or panel on a screen, such as a recommended plan. | Several highlighted items compete for attention; state, status or selection needs a badge, chip or the component's own selected style. | badges (core), cards (core), buttons (core) | css-only |
| [Message](../components/message.md) | Show a conversation as messages from people or an assistant, aligned by sender. | Short app feedback needs a snackbar; a list of conversations needs a list. | snackbar (core), lists (core), cards (core) | css-only |
| [Message scroller](../components/message-scroller.md) | Scroll a conversation that receives messages or streamed replies, or open a saved transcript at its last turn. | A short static exchange needs no scroller; a feed of unrelated items needs a list or the scroll-area utility. | message, lists (core) | auto-init |
| [Pull-to-refresh](../components/pull-to-refresh.md) | Let people fetch the latest items of a feed, inbox or list on a touch screen, with a button that does the same for everyone else. | Content that updates itself, or a page where a pull would compete with another vertical drag; use a refresh button alone. | message-scroller, lists (core) | auto-init |
| [Swipe actions](../components/swipe-actions.md) | Give each row of an inbox, task or file list a few quick actions, such as archive or delete, without a toolbar on every row. | Rows whose actions people need all the time, or a single primary action; show the buttons in the row or use a menu. | lists (core), menu (core) | auto-init |
| [Show more](../components/show-more.md) | A description, review or message that usually runs past a few lines, in a card or list where the full text would push the rest of the layout down. | Sections with headings or controls a person needs to find; use an accordion, whose panels the browser's find-in-page can open.; Text that is short or always matters in full; show all of it. | accordion (core), cards (core) | auto-init |
| [Stat](../components/stat.md) | Summarize a few key figures, each with a label and an optional change, at the top of a dashboard. | Many rows of comparable records need a data table; a trend over time needs a chart. | data-table (core), cards (core), kpi | css-only |
| [Description list](../components/description-list.md) | Show the fields of one record, such as an order's status, address and total, as labelled values people read rather than edit. | Many records compared side by side need a data table; a few headline numbers need stat tiles; editable values need form fields. | stat, data-table (core), lists (core) | css-only |
| [KPI](../components/kpi.md) | Feature a headline figure on a dashboard with its change, a short trend and a line of context or an action. | Several figures with no chart or actions read better as a stats row; a trend the reader has to inspect needs a full chart. | stat, line-chart, cards (core) | css-only |
| [Countdown](../components/countdown.md) | Show a small whole number that changes in place, such as seconds left, a clock or a live count, and draw the eye to each change. | A labelled key figure needs a stat tile; progress toward a goal needs a progress indicator; numbers above 999 or with decimals need plain text. | stat, progress (core), badges (core) | css-only |
| [Timeline](../components/timeline.md) | Show what happened and when, in order, such as order tracking or an activity feed. | Steps the user still has to complete need a stepper; a live conversation needs messages. | stepper, lists (core), message | css-only |
| [Calendar](../components/calendar.md) | Show a month of days with events people scan by date, such as bookings or a team schedule.; Show a week or a day as an hourly grid where each event covers its start and length. | Picking one date for a field needs the date picker; an ordered list of dated events needs a timeline. | date-picker (core), timeline, data-table (core) | css-only |
| [Line chart](../components/line-chart.md) | Show how one or a few measures change over an ordered axis such as months or days, with exact values a hover or a key press away. | Readers need to compare exact values across many rows or sort them; use a data table. A single headline figure needs a stat tile, optionally with a sparkline. | column-chart, data-table (core), stat, mixed-chart | auto-init |
| [Column chart](../components/column-chart.md) | Compare amounts across a handful of categories or periods, such as revenue per month or signups per plan, where the reader judges heights against zero. | The point is the trend's shape over many periods; use a line chart. Readers need exact values across many rows or sorting; use a data table. A single headline figure needs a stat tile. | bar-chart, line-chart, data-table (core), stat, mixed-chart | auto-init |
| [Bar chart](../components/bar-chart.md) | Compare amounts across categories with long labels or a ranked order, such as visitors by source, or show one total split into parts against a limit. | The categories are periods; use a column chart, or a line chart for a trend. Readers need exact values across many rows or sorting; use a data table. | column-chart, line-chart, data-table (core), stat, pie-chart | auto-init |
| [Pie chart](../components/pie-chart.md) | Show how one total splits into a few parts, such as revenue by plan or leads by source, when the shares matter more than exact differences. | There are more than about five parts or the parts are close in size; use a bar chart. The values do not add up to a meaningful whole, or change over time; use a column or line chart. | bar-chart, column-chart, data-table (core), stat, radial-chart | auto-init |
| [Heatmap chart](../components/heatmap-chart.md) | Show where values run high or low across two categories, such as visits by day and hour or activity by week, when the pattern matters more than exact values. | Readers need to compare exact values, or one category has a single row; use a data table or a bar chart. Values change over a continuous time series; use a line chart. | data-table (core), bar-chart, column-chart, line-chart | auto-init |
| [Radar chart](../components/radar-chart.md) | Compare a profile of five to eight measures that share one scale, such as skill or satisfaction scores, for one or a few subjects. | The measures use different units or scales, exact differences matter, or there are more than three series; use a bar or column chart. The rows are a sequence such as months; use a line chart. | bar-chart, column-chart, line-chart, data-table (core) | auto-init |
| [Radial chart](../components/radial-chart.md) | Show how far one to four measures are toward a goal or limit, such as plan targets, capacity or a score. | The values are parts of one whole; use a pie chart. More than about four measures, or close comparisons, need a bar chart. A running task's progress needs a progress indicator. | pie-chart, bar-chart, progress (core), stat | auto-init |
| [Mixed chart](../components/mixed-chart.md) | Compare a measure with a target or a related measure on the same rows, such as revenue against a target line or spend against conversions. | Every series is the same kind; use a line or column chart. Two scales on one plot invite false comparisons, so when the series are unrelated, draw two charts. | line-chart, column-chart, data-table (core) | auto-init |
| [Scatter chart](../components/scatter-chart.md) | Show how two numeric measures relate across many items, such as weight against fuel economy or ad spend against signups. | The x values are categories or dates in order; use a line or column chart. A handful of items reads better as a table or bar chart. | line-chart, bar-chart, data-table (core) | auto-init |
| [Funnel chart](../components/funnel-chart.md) | Show how many people or items reach each step of an ordered process, such as visits, signups and purchases, and the share of the first step each keeps. | The rows are not steps in order; use a bar chart. Values that add up to a whole read better as a pie chart. | bar-chart, pie-chart, data-table (core) | auto-init |
| [Sankey chart](../components/sankey-chart.md) | Show how a quantity splits and merges between stages, such as energy from sources to uses. | The stages form one narrowing path, or flows loop back; use a bar chart or a table. | bar-chart, pie-chart, data-table (core) | auto-init |
| [Treemap chart](../components/treemap-chart.md) | Show how a total splits across many parts, such as a budget across teams or disk space across folders, where a pie would run out of room for slices. | Readers need to compare values precisely or the parts have an order; use a bar or column chart. Two to five parts read better as a pie chart. | pie-chart, bar-chart, data-table (core) | auto-init |
| [Organization chart](../components/org-chart.md) | Show who reports to whom for a team or company of a few dozen people, with a face and a name on each card. | Hundreds of people or a search for one person need a searchable list or table; a deep hierarchy of pages or files needs a tree. | tree, lists (core), data-table (core) | native |
| [Popover](../components/popover.md) | Show a short note or a few actions on press, next to the button, until the user dismisses it. | A hint on hover or focus needs a tooltip; a choice of commands needs a menu; a task to finish needs a dialog. | tooltips (core), menu (core), dialogs (core) | native |
| [Skeleton](../components/skeleton.md) | Hold the layout of content whose shape is known while it loads. | A short wait with no known layout needs a loading indicator; measurable progress needs a progress indicator. | loading-indicator (core), progress (core) | css-only |
| [Empty state](../components/empty-state.md) | Explain why a list, search or view has nothing to show and offer the next step. | An error after an action needs inline feedback or a snackbar; a loading view needs a skeleton or loading indicator. | snackbar (core), skeleton, cards (core) | css-only |
| [Hover card](../components/hover-card.md) | Preview where a link goes, such as a person, repository or article, for people who hover or tab to it, when the linked page holds the same content. | A short label for a control needs a tooltip; content touch users must reach, or anything to act on, belongs in the page, a popover opened by a button or a dialog. | tooltips (core), popover | auto-init |
| [Tour](../components/tour.md) | Introduce new or changed parts of an interface in a short sequence the user starts and can leave at any time. | One hint beside one control needs a popover or tooltip; content people must read needs to stay on the page. | popover, tooltips (core), dialogs (core) | shared-runtime |
| [Loading overlay](../components/loading-overlay.md) | Hold a form, card or panel still while it saves or reloads, so nobody edits or presses what is about to change. | Content that stays usable while it updates, or a wait for the whole page; show a loading indicator or skeleton without blocking input. | loading-indicator (core), skeleton, progress (core) | auto-init |
| [Marquee](../components/marquee.md) | Show a long, decorative set of logos, photos or short slogans in a small space, such as customer logos on a landing page. | People need to read, compare or act on the items; a list, grid or carousel lets them do it at their own pace. Urgent messages need an alert or snackbar. | carousel (core), lists (core), chips (core) | css-only |
| [Image compare](../components/image-compare.md) | Let people compare two images of the same scene, such as before and after an edit. | Several unrelated images need a carousel; one image with detail needs a lightbox. | carousel (core), lightbox, slider (core) | shared-runtime |
| [Confetti](../components/confetti.md) | Mark a rare moment of success the person worked toward, such as a finished purchase, a completed goal or a first published post. | Routine saves, frequent actions and errors; repeated bursts lose their meaning and distract. Confetti never replaces a text confirmation such as a snackbar. | snackbar (core), empty-state, aura | auto-init |
| [Particles](../components/particles.md) | Give a hero, landing section or sign-in panel a sense of depth and movement behind short, high-contrast content. | Behind dense text, forms or data, and on pages that already animate; the motion competes with reading. Never carry meaning in the dots. | aura, confetti, marquee | auto-init |
| [Lightbox](../components/lightbox.md) | Enlarge an image on activation. | Tasks need dialogs; browsing collections needs carousel. | carousel (core), dialogs (core) | auto-init |
| [Map](../components/map.md) | Show where things are when position matters to the task, such as stores near the reader, a delivery route or live vehicles. | A single address or a list the reader scans by name; write the address in text and link to a map app. Never make the map the only way to reach the information it shows. | lists (core), data-table (core), cards (core) | manual |
| [Command palette](../components/command-palette.md) | Let people find and run any of many commands or destinations by typing, from anywhere in the app. | Searching content needs search; a few actions for one item need a menu. | search (core), menu (core), dialogs (core) | auto-init |
| [Input mask](../components/input-mask.md) | A field whose value has a fixed shape people know, such as a phone, card or postal code number, and that reads better grouped as they type. | Values whose length or grouping varies, such as names, international phone numbers or amounts; leave the field plain and validate it with pattern. | text-fields (core), keypad | auto-init |
| [Currency input](../components/currency-input.md) | A field for an amount of money in one known currency, such as a price, budget or payment amount, that should read in the visitor's locale. | Quantities without a currency, or a field whose currency people choose; use a number field, or a select beside a plain text field. | text-fields (core), input-mask | auto-init |
| [Rich text editor](../components/rich-text-editor.md) | Let people write formatted content such as posts, release notes or comments, and submit it as HTML with a form. | Plain text needs a text field; code or Markdown source needs a plain textarea. | text-fields (core), toolbars (core) | manual |
| [Drop zone](../components/drop-zone.md) | Let people choose or drag in files where uploading is the main task of the view. | A form field that takes one optional file needs the compact file input. | text-fields (core), cards (core) | shared-runtime |
| [Tree select](../components/tree-select.md) | Choose one or more leaves from a hierarchy, such as places or categories. | Options one level deep, which a select with optgroups shows, or a tree people browse, which a tree of links shows. | select (core), tree, autocomplete (core) | auto-init |
| [Cascader](../components/cascader.md) | A path through a known hierarchy of a few levels, such as country, region and city, where the server needs every level. | A flat list or one level of groups, which a select covers, a deep or searchable hierarchy, or several paths at once. | select (core), tree | auto-init |
| [Transfer list](../components/transfer-list.md) | Let people pick several options from a long set and see their picks as a list of their own, in the order they chose them. | A short set of options people pick in place; use checkboxes, filter chips or a multiple select. | checkboxes (core), chips (core), select (core), autocomplete (core) | shared-runtime |
| [Rating](../components/rating.md) | Ask for or show a score on a short fixed scale, such as one to five stars. | A continuous value needs a slider; a yes or no answer needs a switch or checkbox. | radio-buttons (core), slider (core) | css-only |
| [Color swatches](../components/color-swatches.md) | Offer a short fixed set of colors, such as a label, theme or calendar color, with an optional custom value. | Any color at all needs the native color input on its own; choosing between named options that are not colors needs radio buttons or chips. | radio-buttons (core), chips (core), text-fields (core) | css-only |
| [Color picker](../components/color-picker.md) | Let someone choose an arbitrary color in the page, such as a brand or highlight color, with keyboard and pointer. | A short fixed palette needs color swatches; a form that only needs a value can keep the native color input alone. | color-swatches, text-fields (core), slider (core) | auto-init |

A few large stages with several fields each, such as a checkout, need a stepper. | fieldsets (core), stepper, radio-buttons (core), checkboxes (core) | auto-init |
